 Klopp's Germany Routs Netherlands to Reach Nations League Quarterfinals
 Ha Seong-nyong 
 Seoul 
 Published 
 2026.11.17 08:24 
 View 
 View Count 
 Enlarge image 
 ▲ German players celebrate the team's 4th goal scored by Florian Wirtz (No. 17) 
 Germany, led by manager Jurgen Klopp, defeated the Netherlands in a landslide victory to secure a spot in the UEFA Nations League quarterfinals. 
 Germany triumphed over the Netherlands with a 5-0 scoreline in their final Group 2 Matchday 6 home fixture of the 2026-2027 UEFA Nations League League A held at the Olympiastadion in Berlin, Germany. 
 With this result, Germany finished the group stage with 3 wins, 2 draws, and 1 loss, accumulating 11 points—level with the Netherlands and Greece, which defeated Serbia 1-0 on the same day. 
 In UNL League A, 16 countries compete across 4 groups, with the top 2 teams from each group advancing to the quarterfinals. 
 When teams are tied on points, head-to-head records are used as the tiebreaker. 
 Since Germany, the Netherlands, and Greece all finished with 5 points in head-to-head matches, unable to be separated, goal difference in head-to-head matches was applied. Germany claimed 1st place with +4, the Netherlands took 2nd with +2, and Greece placed 3rd with -6. 
 Germany, which secured consecutive wins and advanced to the quarterfinals following a 3-1 victory over Serbia on November 14, achieved its first back-to-back wins under manager Jurgen Klopp, who took the helm after Julian Nagelsmann was dismissed following the team's elimination in the Round of 32 at the 2026 FIFA World Cup. 
 Germany recorded 1 draw and 1 loss in Klopp's first two matches in charge against the Netherlands and Greece in September, but has since remained undefeated with 3 wins and 1 draw across 4 matches in October and November. 
 Enlarge image 
 The match also marked the most goals scored and the largest margin of victory since Klopp took charge. 
 The Netherlands, which had been leading the group prior to this match, suffered a heavy defeat and dropped to 2nd place, but successfully joined Germany in advancing to the quarterfinals. 
 The quarterfinals will take place in March next year, with the matchups to be determined via a draw at a later date. 
 Germany opened the scoring in the 41st minute of the first half with a winning goal by Derry Scherhant. 
 Scherhant, who made his international debut during October's A-match period after being selected by manager Klopp and played his 4th match on this day, received a pass from Joshua Kimmich, penetrated the left side of the penalty area, and fired a right-footed shot to score his debut goal for the national team. 
 Ending the first half with a one-goal lead, Germany extended their advantage in the 15th minute of the second half when Florian Wirtz struck a left-footed mid-range shot from the right side of the penalty arc into the back of the net. 
 In the 20th minute of the second half, Nico Schlotterbeck scored the team's third goal with a diving header from a free-kick situation. 
 Germany then sealed the victory with additional goals from Wirtz in the 26th minute of the second half and Brajan Gruda in the 32nd minute of the second half.
